RECURRING FINDINGS (2+ samples, or spec-caused). A. LOW, signature, spec-caused, 3 of 3: the tote's sides step outward at about two-thirds height, from the shipped grid (S0 drawings/products-canvas-field-tote-d3.png; S1 and S2 products-canvas-field-tote-desktop-light.png). It still reads as a bag next to the 'Bags' label and the day pack and duffel, so the score stays at 4. B. LOW, signature, 2 of 3 (S0 and S2): commerce product banners use one lead building per category, 4 instead of 11. Each product varies the arrangement, so no two screens are identical, but every bag page leads with the same 'BAGS' shop (S2 products-canvas-field-tote-desktop-light.png) and every apparel page with the same purple 'COAT' shop. In S2 that puts 'COAT' over the Merino Crew Sweater page (S2 drawings/products-merino-crew-sweater-d1.png). S2 agent-report.md line 34 lists it under 'couldn't apply'. S1 gives every product its own building ('WOOL' mill for the sweater, a forge for the skillet; S1 agent-report.md line 7, drawings/products-merino-crew-sweater-d1.png). The spec says 'its own Banner' (dist/agent.md line 335), which agents read as its own arrangement. The reference has no store to compare with; its scenes change subject (p1-i1.png vs p2-i2.png). C. LOW, content, worse than published, spec-allowed, 3 of 3: commerce product-card summaries clamp at 2 lines and cut mid-phrase ('Water-resistant backpack for commutes and short…', 'A sturdy steel mug for coffee at home or…', 'A simple loop of vegetable-tanned…') in S0, S1 and S2 home-desktop-light.png. Published 1.1.0 showed them whole in 3 lines in the same 5-column cards (1.1.0-rc.2 commerce/screenshots/home-desktop-light.png). The rc.6 Card rule keeps the 2-line clamp for product cards. Nothing breaks: the name, category and price lead, and the full text is on the detail page. So it stays at 4 for hierarchy, but it is a regression with a prompt fix. D. COMPARED WITH PUBLISHED 1.1.0. Better in 3 of 3: the tote (published read as a padlock under one arch, 1.1.0-rc.2 commerce/screenshots/home-desktop-light.png card 1), the sweater (published had detached sleeves), the coat (published read as a grid), the key ring (published read as a magnifier), detail sprites, hero identity and blog scene variety. Equal in 3 of 3: blog summaries, category icons, the settings two-column form, banner lead height (105–119px vs about 117px), the dashboard layout and the filter row. Worse in 2+ samples: only C, the commerce card summaries clamped at 2 lines (3 of 3). Published shows them whole. Low impact.

SIGNATURE (4). Present in all four apps in 3 of 3 and placed as Applying says. Blog: a full-bleed hero with a framed title window, a lit post office on a rimmed rise, a diagonal path, a moon, stars and drifting clouds. Articles and about each have their own banner and lead. Store: the grid, cart and every product page have a strip or banner with a lead. Dashboard and settings: one strip per screen (a server yard; a workshop with a gear plate). Empty states have vignettes (S1 blog state-search-empty, S2 dashboard state-empty-filter), and the checkered ground strip runs on every screen. Motion is stepped. S2 motion-m1.png shows nc-drift at 120000ms with steps(30); the cloud moves between frames, and the nav marker blinks on and off across frames. Grid sprites are 41–47% visible ink in 3 of 3 and read as their products. Why not 5: the tote's step-out sides (A, 3 of 3, spec-caused); banners repeat one building per category in 2 of 3 (B); strip props are small and simpler than the reference's figure and snow-laden trees at the same scale (S1 commerce/drawings/cart-d1.png vs reference/illustrations/p2-i2.png).

OTHER SCORES. Reference fidelity (4), 3 of 3: a night ground, cream pixel type, 4px windows, dither rules under h2s, one gold commit with a hard shadow, the gold ▶ marker, hue top bars and bullets, block meters and the checkered grass strip, as in reference/screenshots/p1-desktop-light.png and p1-i1.png, without the reference's cabin, figure or snow. Cross-app consistency (4): one family in all three samples. Dashboard and settings use a sidebar in 3 of 3, while blog and commerce use top navigation. Small drift: S2 commerce boxes the filter row in a panel (S2 home-desktop-light.png) and S0 and S1 do not. Hierarchy (4): scene and h1 first, then ruled h2s; 48px KPIs lead the dashboard; the 48px price and gold Add to cart lead the product page; blog summaries are whole. The weak spot is the clamped commerce card summaries (C). Spacing (4): the 4px scale and h2 rhythm hold; the settings form fills its window in 3 of 3; detail windows are balanced in 2 of 3. The voids in F and G are one-offs. Component states (4): a gold focus frame on the first invalid field, danger frames with '!' messages (S2 commerce state-checkout-errors-desktop-light.png); a titled dialog with a framed close, Cancel and gold Confirm change (S1 settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-light.png); empty results with a vignette, a 0-of-n meter and a framed ▶ Clear filters (S1 blog state-search-empty, S2 dashboard state-empty-filter). Polish (4): radius 0, 2/4px borders, no default-browser leftovers and no generic look in any sample.

BAR: seven 4s, average 4.0, none below 3, across three samples. The confirm step PASSES and the candidate can go to human review. Update goal: reached in 3 of 3. All seven rc.5 recurring findings are fixed in 3 of 3. Every earlier tracked item is fixed in every sample checked (3 of 3 for most; mobile wordmark and mobile table in the 2 of 3 opened). The only regression from published is the 2-line clamp on commerce card summaries (3 of 3, low). The other recurring items are low: the tote's step-out sides (3 of 3, spec-caused), one banner building per category (2 of 3) and the report-table process gap (harness limit).
